title: Unify micro-interactions, density scales, and token sets for Console dashboards, rollouts, and cost views
creator: Maya Patel
description: Audit and converge divergent component states and interaction patterns used across the Console dashboard, Rollouts page, and Cost Insights. Deliver a single Figma token scale and micro-interaction spec (hover, focus, loading states, skeletons) plus updated component instances so engineers can ship consistent behavior and visuals across hosted/dedicated/private views.
acceptance_criteria: A single token scale (spacing, type, elevation, radius, motion durations) reviewed and approved by Design and Engineering
Figma library updated with revised Metric Card, Action Banner, Table Row, and Empty State components with standardized interaction states
Prototype demonstrating dashboard -> rollout -> cost-view transitions with consistent micro-interactions and accessible focus outlines
Engineers have a referenced GitHub PR and implementation checklist; QA signoff on visual/regression tests
Documentation added to Console Design System Confluence page with migration notes and rollout plan
updates: 2025-10-15: Created ticket. Initial scope drafted after cross-functional sync with PM (Aria Gomez) and Eng (Jamal Ruiz). Key pain points collected: inconsistent card paddings, multiple loading skeletons, differing button affordances on rollout banners.

2025-10-18: Exploratory audit completed. Inventory attached: 18 distinct component variants across dashboard, rollouts, and cost views. Collected screenshots and CSS token exports from the current console (see attachments).

2025-10-22: Workshop with Research and Accessibility. Decided on four density breakpoints (compact, standard, comfortable, expanded) and motion scale (fast/medium/slow) to match performance SLOs and user needs.

2025-10-27: First Figma iteration uploaded: 'DDS: MetricCard v2' and 'DDS: ActionBanner v1'. Linked prototype includes transitions; noted performance caveat for streaming responses in low-bandwidth mode.

2025-10-30: Internal design review. PM (Aria Gomez) approved token scale. Engineering flagged two constraints: table virtualization impacts row hover animation; KV cache latency may make some transitions janky in Dedicated. Marked follow-up to provide degraded interaction guidelines.

2025-11-01: Created GitHub PR #1421 in console-ui repo with CSS token mappings and a demo story in Storybook (placeholder components). Requesting eng review: @jamal-ruiz. Added implementation checklist to PR description.

2025-11-02: Submitted ticket for Design Leadership review. Early accessibility pass completed; focus-visible styles meet contrast requirements. Awaiting final sign-off and scheduling of canary rollout with PM/Eng.
review_feedback: Aria Gomez (PM): Love the density scale — please add a short migration note for customers on Dedicated about temporary visual regressions during capacity migration.
Jamal Ruiz (Eng): Prefer simpler 150ms motion for hover to avoid excess GPU churn; flagged table row hover for desktop only. Will implement reduced-motion media query support.
Priya Sharma (Accessibility): Focus ring contrast is good; recommend increasing hit area for metric cards to 44px min for touch devices.
Design Lead (Owen Park): Consolidate token names to the new 'rd_' prefix and avoid legacy 'console-' tokens. Also request a small token mapping table in Confluence for quick reference.
design_decisions: Adopt 4 density tiers to give product teams explicit control over information density across deployments
Motion durations standardized to 80ms (fast), 150ms (medium), 260ms (slow); default interactions use 150ms to balance perceived responsiveness and GPU overhead
Metric Card will adopt a primary and secondary token set: rd-space-2/4/8, rd-elevation-1/2, rd-radius-2; use these across dashboards and rollout banners
Loading skeletons unified to a single shimmer pattern and a reduced variant for low-bandwidth fallbacks
Fallback interaction spec: if KV cache latency > X ms, transition to 'reduced motion + skeleton-only' to avoid layout jank
next_steps: Address Engineering feedback in GitHub PR #1421 and update Storybook stories with virtualization-aware examples
Publish Confluence migration guide that includes token mapping table and example overrides for Dedicated customers
Schedule a cross-team demo the week of 2025-11-10 to walk through prototype and rollout plan
Create DES-9343 to cover iconography audit for metric cards and DES-9344 to track rollout of the reduced-motion feature flag
Collect a small pilot group (2 customers) for canary verification after the UI change lands to validate no regressions in cost dashboards
